# Issue #13: Use git worktrees to isolate concurrent agent sessions ## Problem Summary When `max_concurrent_prs` > 1, the [engineering_dispatcher.py](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py) spawns multiple LLM agent sessions that all operate in the **same** `REPO_DIR`. This causes: 1. **Branch cross-contamination** — Agent B checks out its branch while Agent A has uncommitted edits; git carries over the dirty working tree. 2. **Lost work** — Agent A's branch is switched out from under it, causing test failures or lost changes. 3. **Incorrect commits** — Agent B commits Agent A's files into the wrong PR. ## Current State The infrastructure for worktrees is **partially built but never wired into the dispatcher**: | Component | Status | |-----------|--------| | [config.json](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/config.json) `worktree_path` field | ✅ Exists (set to `…-bug-fixer-worktree`) | | [configure.sh](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/configure.sh#L398-L438) Step 6 | ✅ Creates a single static worktree | | [README.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/README.md) docs | ✅ Mentions dedicated worktree operation | | [engineering_dispatcher.py](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py) | ❌ **Never uses** `worktree_path` — always passes `REPO_DIR` | | [SKILL.md](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/skills/bug-fixer-engineering/SKILL.md) | ❌ Says "Work in: `REPO_DIR`" — no worktree awareness | The existing single static worktree would still collide when multiple agents run concurrently — it's the same problem shifted to a different directory. **We need per-issue ephemeral worktrees.** --- ## Proposed Approach ### Design: Per-Issue Ephemeral Worktrees Each spawned agent session gets its own `git worktree`, created by the dispatcher before spawning and cleaned up after the PR is opened (or on failure). The worktree lifecycle is entirely owned by the dispatcher and liveness system — agents never create or destroy worktrees. ### Architecture Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR D["engineering_dispatcher.py"] -->|1. git worktree add| WT1["worktrees/issue-42/"] D -->|2. git worktree add| WT2["worktrees/issue-57/"] D -->|3. agentapi new-conversation| A1["Agent 1
cwd: issue-42/"] D -->|4. agentapi new-conversation| A2["Agent 2
cwd: issue-57/"] A1 -->|5. PR opened| PR1["PR #100"] A2 -->|6. PR opened| PR2["PR #101"] D -->|7. git worktree remove| WT1 D -->|8. git worktree remove| WT2 ``` ### Changes Required #### 1. `engineering_dispatcher.py` — Core worktree lifecycle **Create worktree** (before spawning each agent): ```python WORKTREES_DIR = STATE_DIR / "worktrees" def create_worktree(issue_num: int, branch_name: str) -> Path: """Create an ephemeral worktree for a specific issue.""" wt_path = WORKTREES_DIR / f"issue-{issue_num}" if wt_path.exists(): # Stale worktree from previous failed run — clean it up remove_worktree(wt_path) WORKTREES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "add", str(wt_path), "-b", branch_name, "origin/main"], check=False) if r.returncode != 0: # Fallback: create worktree at detached HEAD, agent will checkout r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(wt_path), "origin/main"], check=True) return wt_path def remove_worktree(wt_path: Path): """Remove a worktree and prune.""" run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(wt_path)], check=False) run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "prune"], check=False) ``` **Wire into spawn paths** — Every place that builds a prompt must: 1. Create a worktree 2. Replace `Work in: {REPO_DIR}` with `Work in: {wt_path}` 3. Store the worktree path in the claim/lock file 4. Record the worktree path in the dispatch tracking file There are **three spawn paths** that need updating: | Spawn Path | Lines | Type | |---|---|---| | Step 1: Reattach orphaned issues | [L274-L294](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py#L274-L294) | `reattach` | | Step 2.5: PR iteration dispatch | [L390-L447](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py#L390-L447) | `pr_iteration` | | Step 4: Fresh fix dispatch | [L523-L562](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/engineering_dispatcher.py#L523-L562) | `fresh_fix` | > [!IMPORTANT] > PR iteration dispatches (Step 2.5) also need a worktree, but should check out the **existing PR branch** rather than creating a new branch from `origin/main`. **Clean up worktrees** — Add cleanup in two places: a. **On successful completion** (in [liveness.py `sweep_dispatches`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/liveness.py#L504-L508)): When `_check_success()` returns True, remove the worktree before deleting the dispatch file. b. **On recovery** (in [liveness.py `_recover`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/liveness.py#L411-L479)): When a dispatch is abandoned after failed resume attempts, remove the worktree. c. **Stale worktree sweep** (new, in dispatcher startup): Scan `WORKTREES_DIR` for directories that don't have a corresponding active claim or dispatch file, and prune them. #### 2. Lock file schema update Add `worktree_path` to the claim lock file so recovery knows which worktree to clean up: ```json { "issue": 42, "dispatcher_pid": 12345, "conversation_id": "abc-123", "claimed_at": "2026-10-01T...", "worktree_path": "/path/to/.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/worktrees/issue-42" } ``` #### 3. Dispatch record schema update Add `worktree_path` to `record_dispatch()` kwargs so `sweep_dispatches` can clean up: ```python record_dispatch(DISPATCHES_DIR, new_conv_id, "fresh_fix", issue_number=issue_num, timeout_minutes=45, worktree_path=str(wt_path)) ``` #### 4. `skills/bug-fixer-engineering/SKILL.md` updates - Step 6 (Branch): Update to reflect that the dispatcher already created the branch inside the worktree. The agent should **not** run `git checkout -b` — the branch is already checked out. - Step 11 (Push): Push works the same from within the worktree — no changes needed. - Remove references to "Work in: REPO_DIR" — the prompt will say the worktree path. - Add a note: "Do NOT create or destroy git worktrees — the dispatcher manages worktree lifecycle." #### 5. `configure.sh` update The existing Step 6 creates a single static worktree at `worktree_path`. This should be rethought: - **Option A (recommended)**: Remove the static worktree creation entirely. The dispatcher creates ephemeral worktrees on demand. The `worktree_path` config field becomes the **parent directory** for ephemeral worktrees (default: `{STATE_DIR}/worktrees`). - **Option B**: Keep the static worktree as a fallback for `max_concurrent_prs: 1` mode (simpler, lower risk). #### 6. `pre_tool_gate.py` awareness [`pre_tool_gate.py`](file:///Users/mcneillm/Documents/Projects/bug-fixer-loop-plugin/scripts/pre_tool_gate.py#L276) already handles worktrees in `_git_dir()` — it calls `git rev-parse --git-dir` which correctly resolves inside worktrees. No changes needed here, but verify the `repo_dir` derivation works when the agent's cwd is a worktree subpath. --- ## Risk Assessment | Risk | Severity | Mitigation | |------|----------|------------| | Orphaned worktrees consume disk space | Medium | Stale worktree sweep at dispatcher startup + `git worktree prune` | | Worktree creation fails (lock contention) | Low | Fallback to `--detach` mode; circuit breaker already handles spawn failures | | Agent tries to operate outside its worktree | Medium | Prompt explicitly says "Work in: {wt_path}" — same pattern already used for REPO_DIR | | Existing `worktree_path` config field semantics change | Low | Backward compatible: if field is empty, use default `STATE_DIR/worktrees` | | Multiple agents pushing to same remote concurrently | Low | Each agent pushes a different branch — no conflict at the git remote level | | Worktree `.git` file confuses tools/scripts | Low | `pre_tool_gate.py` already handles this correctly | --- ## Implementation Order 1. **Add worktree helper functions** to `engineering_dispatcher.py` (`create_worktree`, `remove_worktree`, `sweep_stale_worktrees`) 2. **Update the three spawn paths** to create worktrees and pass worktree paths in prompts 3. **Update lock file and dispatch record schemas** to include `worktree_path` 4. **Update `liveness.py`** to clean up worktrees on success and recovery 5. **Update `SKILL.md`** to reflect the new worktree-based workflow 6. **Update `configure.sh`** to align `worktree_path` semantics 7. **Add tests** for worktree creation, cleanup, and stale sweep 8. **Update docs** (`README.md`, `plugin-architecture.md`) --- ## Open Questions 1. **Should `max_concurrent_prs: 1` still use a worktree?** Using worktrees even for single-agent mode provides safety if the user is also working in the repo. Recommend: yes, always use worktrees. 2. **Where should worktrees live?** Two options: - `STATE_DIR/worktrees/` (inside `.agents/plugins/...`) — keeps everything together, but adds `.agents` to git's worktree list - Sibling directory to repo (e.g., `{repo}-worktrees/`) — cleaner git state, but requires filesystem access outside the repo 3. **Should we pre-create the branch or let the agent do it?** Pre-creating (dispatcher does `git worktree add -b branch origin/main`) is cleaner — the agent just starts coding. But for reattach/iteration, the branch already exists, so we need `git worktree add wt_path existing-branch` instead.

# Issue #13: Use git worktrees to isolate concurrent agent sessions ## Problem Summary When `max_concurrent_prs` > 1, the `engineering_dispatcher.py` spawns multiple LLM agent sessions that all operate in the **same** `REPO_DIR`. This causes: 1. **Branch cross-contamination** — Agent B checks out its branch while Agent A has uncommitted edits; git carries over the dirty working tree. 2. **Lost work** — Agent A's branch is switched out from under it, causing test failures or lost changes. 3. **Incorrect commits** — Agent B commits Agent A's files into the wrong PR. ## Current State The infrastructure for worktrees is **partially built but never wired into the dispatcher**: | Component | Status | |-----------|--------| | `config.json` `worktree_path` field | ✅ Exists (set during configure) | | `configure.sh` Step 6 | ✅ Creates a single static worktree | | `README.md` docs | ✅ Mentions dedicated worktree operation | | `engineering_dispatcher.py` | ❌ **Never uses** `worktree_path` — always passes `REPO_DIR` | | `SKILL.md` | ❌ Says "Work in: `REPO_DIR`" — no worktree awareness | The existing single static worktree would still collide when multiple agents run concurrently — it's the same problem shifted to a different directory. **We need per-issue ephemeral worktrees.** --- ## Proposed Approach ### Design: Per-Issue Ephemeral Worktrees Each spawned agent session gets its own `git worktree`, created by the dispatcher before spawning and cleaned up after the PR is opened (or on failure). The worktree lifecycle is entirely owned by the dispatcher and liveness system — agents never create or destroy worktrees. ### Worktree Location Worktrees live at **`/worktrees/`** — inside the consuming repo root, not inside the plugin directory structure. This is critical because: 1. **Stays within `workspace_uris` boundary** — the sidecar's `agent_permissions.workspace_uris` points to the repo root (`file://`). Worktrees inside this boundary don't trigger Antigravity's permission prompt for editing files outside the project. 2. **Clean separation** — the plugin directory (`.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop/`) contains code; the workspace directory (`.agents/plugins/bug-fixer-loop-workspace/`) contains runtime state like claims and dispatches; worktrees are full working copies and belong at the repo level. ``` myrepo/ ← REPO_DIR (workspace_uris root) ├── .agents/plugins/ │ ├── bug-fixer-loop/ ← plugin code (symlinked) │ └── bug-fixer-loop-workspace/ ← runtime state │ ├── config.json │ ├── claims/ │ └── dispatches/ ├── worktrees/ ← ephemeral agent worktrees │ ├── issue-42/ ← full working copy for agent A │ └── issue-57/ ← full working copy for agent B ├── src/ └── .gitignore ← must include "worktrees/" ``` Path derivation in the dispatcher: ```python REPO_DIR = STATE_DIR.parent.parent.parent # already exists (line 168) WORKTREES_DIR = REPO_DIR / "worktrees" # at repo root ``` ### Architecture Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR D["engineering_dispatcher.py"] -->|"1. git worktree add"| WT1["worktrees/issue-42/"] D -->|"2. git worktree add"| WT2["worktrees/issue-57/"] D -->|"3. agentapi new-conversation"| A1["Agent 1
cwd: worktrees/issue-42/"] D -->|"4. agentapi new-conversation"| A2["Agent 2
cwd: worktrees/issue-57/"] A1 -->|"5. PR opened"| PR1["PR #100"] A2 -->|"6. PR opened"| PR2["PR #101"] D -->|"7. git worktree remove"| WT1 D -->|"8. git worktree remove"| WT2 ``` ### Changes Required #### 1. `engineering_dispatcher.py` — Core worktree lifecycle **Create worktree** (before spawning each agent): ```python WORKTREES_DIR = REPO_DIR / "worktrees" def create_worktree(issue_num: int, branch_name: str) -> Path: """Create an ephemeral worktree for a specific issue.""" wt_path = WORKTREES_DIR / f"issue-{issue_num}" if wt_path.exists(): # Stale worktree from previous failed run — clean it up remove_worktree(wt_path) WORKTREES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "add", str(wt_path), "-b", branch_name, "origin/main"], check=False) if r.returncode != 0: # Fallback: create worktree at detached HEAD, agent will checkout r = run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(wt_path), "origin/main"], check=True) return wt_path def remove_worktree(wt_path: Path): """Remove a worktree and prune.""" run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(wt_path)], check=False) run(["git", "-C", str(REPO_DIR), "worktree", "prune"], check=False) ``` **Wire into spawn paths** — Every place that builds a prompt must: 1. Create a worktree before spawning 2. Replace `Work in: {REPO_DIR}` with `Work in: {wt_path}` 3. Store the worktree path in the claim/lock file 4. Record the worktree path in the dispatch tracking file There are **three spawn paths** that need updating: | Spawn Path | Lines | Type | |---|---|---| | Step 1: Reattach orphaned issues | L274-L294 | `reattach` | | Step 2.5: PR iteration dispatch | L390-L447 | `pr_iteration` | | Step 4: Fresh fix dispatch | L523-L562 | `fresh_fix` | > **Note:** PR iteration dispatches (Step 2.5) need a worktree too, but should check out the **existing PR branch** rather than creating a new branch from `origin/main`. **Clean up worktrees** — Add cleanup in three places: a. **On successful completion** (in `liveness.py` `sweep_dispatches`): When `_check_success()` returns True, remove the worktree before deleting the dispatch file. b. **On recovery** (in `liveness.py` `_recover`): When a dispatch is abandoned after failed resume attempts, remove the worktree. c. **Stale worktree sweep** (new, in dispatcher startup): Scan `WORKTREES_DIR` for directories that don't have a corresponding active claim or dispatch file, and prune them. #### 2. Lock file schema update Add `worktree_path` to the claim lock file so recovery knows which worktree to clean up: ```json { "issue": 42, "dispatcher_pid": 12345, "conversation_id": "abc-123", "claimed_at": "2026-10-01T...", "worktree_path": "/path/to/myrepo/worktrees/issue-42" } ``` #### 3. Dispatch record schema update Add `worktree_path` to `record_dispatch()` kwargs so `sweep_dispatches` can clean up: ```python record_dispatch(DISPATCHES_DIR, new_conv_id, "fresh_fix", issue_number=issue_num, timeout_minutes=45, worktree_path=str(wt_path)) ``` #### 4. `skills/bug-fixer-engineering/SKILL.md` updates - Step 6 (Branch): Update to reflect that the dispatcher already created the branch inside the worktree. The agent should **not** run `git checkout -b` — the branch is already checked out. - Step 11 (Push): Push works the same from within the worktree — no changes needed. - Remove references to "Work in: REPO_DIR" — the prompt will say the worktree path. - Add a note: "Do NOT create or destroy git worktrees — the dispatcher manages worktree lifecycle." #### 5. `configure.sh` / `install.sh` updates - **`install.sh`**: Add `worktrees/` to the consuming repo's root `.gitignore` during installation (append if not already present). - **`configure.sh`**: The existing Step 6 creates a single static worktree at `worktree_path`. This should be removed or repurposed — the dispatcher now creates ephemeral worktrees on demand. The `worktree_path` config field becomes unnecessary (or can remain as a legacy/override). #### 6. `pre_tool_gate.py` awareness `pre_tool_gate.py` already handles worktrees in `_git_dir()` — it calls `git rev-parse --git-dir` which correctly resolves inside worktrees. No code changes needed, but verify the `repo_dir` derivation works when the agent's cwd is a worktree subpath. #### 7. `.gitignore` updates Add `worktrees/` to: - The consuming repo's root `.gitignore` (via `install.sh`) - The workspace `.gitignore` template (for `dispatches/` — already exists at runtime but not gitignored) --- ## Risk Assessment | Risk | Severity | Mitigation | |------|----------|------------| | Orphaned worktrees consume disk space | Medium | Stale worktree sweep at dispatcher startup + `git worktree prune` | | Worktree creation fails (lock contention) | Low | Fallback to `--detach` mode; circuit breaker already handles spawn failures | | Agent tries to operate outside its worktree | Medium | Prompt explicitly says "Work in: {wt_path}" — same pattern already used for REPO_DIR | | Existing `worktree_path` config field semantics change | Low | Backward compatible: field can remain for legacy; dispatcher ignores it in favour of ephemeral worktrees | | Multiple agents pushing to same remote concurrently | Low | Each agent pushes a different branch — no conflict at the git remote level | | Worktree `.git` file confuses tools/scripts | Low | `pre_tool_gate.py` already handles this correctly | --- ## Implementation Order 1. **Add worktree helper functions** to `engineering_dispatcher.py` (`create_worktree`, `remove_worktree`, `sweep_stale_worktrees`) 2. **Update the three spawn paths** to create worktrees and pass worktree paths in prompts 3. **Update lock file and dispatch record schemas** to include `worktree_path` 4. **Update `liveness.py`** to clean up worktrees on success and recovery 5. **Update `SKILL.md`** to reflect the new worktree-based workflow 6. **Update `install.sh`** to add `worktrees/` to the consuming repo's `.gitignore` 7. **Update `configure.sh`** to remove or repurpose the static worktree creation 8. **Add tests** for worktree creation, cleanup, and stale sweep 9. **Update docs** (`README.md`, `plugin-architecture.md`) ## Design Decisions - **Always use worktrees**, even for `max_concurrent_prs: 1` — protects against user working in the repo simultaneously. - **Worktrees at `/worktrees/`**, not inside the plugin dir — stays within `workspace_uris` boundary (no Antigravity permission prompts), clean separation of concerns. - **Dispatcher owns worktree lifecycle** — agents never create or destroy worktrees; they just work inside the provided directory. - **Pre-create branches** — dispatcher does `git worktree add -b origin/main` so the agent starts coding immediately. For reattach/iteration, use `git worktree add `.

├── worktrees/                             ← ephemeral agent worktrees
│   ├── issue-42/
│   └── issue-57/
